context:
Goal: a stalled background job never goes unnoticed, at a stated cost, and watchers come back where their bug is fixed.
Problem (rule): CLAUDE.md rule outcomes-mechanize-rules, line 11, says monitoring runs "never on a timer or on every tool call, and starts no new long-lived process" (added b25883784, 2026-10-22). Its reason is a principle, "watching must cost less than what it watches"; no record gives a bug as the reason. Yet the stall watcher runs a loop per background job today, and you said the watchers were turned off for bugs.
Based on (read): what was turned off, and whether its bug is fixed:
- Monitor tool: denied 2026-09-16, "it errors often" (a5af6d69d). Allowed again 2026-10-11 by decision agents-wait-with-monitor (f58db013f). Its error rate is unmeasured.
- gh run watch: refused since 2026-10-16; one run made 131 GitHub calls in 60 s and merges failed on the rate limit (2b96e1c7c). Replaced by the CI wake hook, which reads every 30-120 s; its real rate is unmeasured.
- Sleep-and-poll waiter: relaxed 2026-10-12 (8a5ff1bfb); its false alarms are still open.
- tail -f: still refused, by principle only (the stream outlives the turn). No bug.
- Agents' leftover watchers: held by an instruction only; the check was dropped after it refused 248 of 1,787 real stops. Not fixed.
- decision-watch Stop row: removed 2026-10-13 (386194af8) because the Stop event might never reach the mod. Fixed in code (1340aa4f0, 93147e97b); no live proof yet.
- Stall watcher: never turned off; advisory; does nothing on Windows.
Based on (ruling): agents-wait-with-monitor, stall-watch, background-needs-end-note. Asked again because CLAUDE.md line 11 still bans what they allow, and you asked whether the bugs are fixed.
Departs from: CLAUDE.md line 11, which bans every timer and long-lived process — c allows one that ends with its job.

lastAnswer.note: Asked: "have we fixed background watchers? remember they were disabled out of buginess not out of disdain". Rewritten 22:39 CST from the coordinator's read of git history.

options.gain: Smallest change; the record tells the truth.
options.how: Rewrite stall-watch's cost line (one watcher per background job, ends with its job, 0.2 s loop) and name it as your exception to line 11.
options.label: Record an exception for the stall watcher only
options.lose: Every other watcher stays banned, bug fixed or not.

options.how: Drop the watcher. The Stop check reads each job's log age once, when the session stops.
options.label: Rework the stall watcher to read on demand
options.lose: A stall is seen only when the session stops, not as it happens.

options.gain: The rule says what your rulings already allow, and Monitor's bug gets a number.
options.how: Rewrite line 11: a watcher may run if it ends with its job and its record states its cost (as agents-wait-with-monitor, stall-watch and background-needs-end-note already allow). A lane measures Monitor's error rate (debt notes line 495).
options.label: Rewrite line 11 to match your rulings; measure Monitor
options.lose: One rule rewrite and one measuring lane.

ref: deep audit 1102, report docs/plans/deep-audit/report.md on audit/deep-1102 (6b6a41f3), table 'claude-settings: homes', row stall-watch-timer-rule
title: Watchers: CLAUDE.md line 11 still bans what your rulings allow. Rewrite it to allow a watcher that ends with its job, and measure Monitor's errors?
why: Recommended: c. Your rulings already allow these watchers; only line 11 lags, and Monitor's "errors often" has never been measured. Also open: decision-watch needs one live proof line, or its Stop row comes back (decision-watch-mod-limits).
